keyframe_review.note: New keyframe (Cliopatria has no row). Spring 1848: the lagoon plus the six Veneto towns the page names; Verona stayed Austrian. The page gives no area. The towns fell back to Austria between 11 and 24 June (and Osoppo on 13 October), leaving Venice alone, as the ledger shows.

correction.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: after the armistice of 9 August 1848 Venice 'was the only city in Lombardy-Venetia which remained in the hands of the insurgents' (First Italian War page); it held out to August 1849 while the Austrians blockaded it and took Fort Marghera (26 May 1849).

region.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

ledger.note: 22 March 1848: Daniele Manin proclaims the Republic of San Marco at Venice. 'independence was declared on 22 March 1848'; the insurrection began on 17 March ('Viva San Marco!' at the Arsenal two days before the declaration); 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'.

region.text: the Veneto towns that sided with Venice: 'Belluno, Padua, Rovigo, Treviso, Udine, and Vicenza' (Verona stayed Austrian)

ledger.note: March 1848: the Veneto towns join Venice. The republic 'extended into most of Venetia'; 'Belluno, Padua, Rovigo, Treviso, Udine, and Vicenza' sided with the lagoon, Verona stayed Austrian. The page does not date each town.

region.text: Udine, 'which surrendered on 22 April after an artillery bombardment'

ledger.note: 22-23 April 1848: Udine surrenders to Nugent's Austrians. First Italian War page: 'Udine which surrendered on 22 April after an artillery bombardment'. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: added/changed from the First Italian War page.]

region.text: Belluno: 'the Austrians entered Belluno on 5 May'

ledger.note: 5 May 1848: the Austrians enter Belluno. First Italian War page: 'the Austrians entered Belluno on 5 May'. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: added/changed from the First Italian War page.]

region.text: Vicenza, Padua, Treviso and Palmanova (Udine province)

ledger.note: 11-24 June 1848: the mainland towns fall to Austria. 'Padua and Treviso fell on 13 June 1848, Vicenza surrendered on 11 June, and Palmanova fell on 24 June.' The page does not name the captor in these sentences.

region.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

ledger.note: 4 July 1848: the Venetian assembly votes union with Sardinia, so Venice passes under the Sardinian crown. 'the Venetian assembly voted 127-6 to approve Manin's proposal of subsumption into the Kingdom of Sardinia' (4 July; the First Italian War page says the parliament accepted annexation on 5 July 1848).

region.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

ledger.note: 9 August 1848: the union ends and Venice is independent again (the land returns from Sardinia). 'On 9 August 1848, Charles Albert signed an armistice that restored the Piedmontese border at the Ticino, ending the union after about a month'; Manin is Dictator in August.

By 9 August 1848 Venice alone was held by the insurgents ('the only city in Lombardy-Venetia which remained in the hands of the insurgents'); the page does not date the return of Rovigo, so this event bridges the silence. Belluno is a separate May event. [Reviewer eu-20-x, 2026-11-01: added/changed from the First Italian War page.]
13 October 1848: Osoppo, the last mainland stronghold, falls. 'Osoppo held out until 13 October 1848.'

region.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

ledger.note: 22-27 August 1849: Venice surrenders after famine and cholera. 'Terms were agreed on 22 August'; 'Radetzky's entrance to Venice on 27 August marked the complete surrender of Venice' (the lead gives 28 August; the Kingdom of Lombardy-Venetia page 24 August).

region.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

ledger.note: August 1849: the Republic of San Marco ends. Radetzky enters Venice on 27 August 1849 and Austrian rule is restored over Lombardy-Venetia.

wars.name: Siege of Venice (1849)

zones.text: Venice and its lagoon: 'Based on the Venetian Lagoon'

wars.outcome: Austria blockaded Venice after the assembly voted on 2 April 1849 to keep fighting, attacked Fort Marghera on 4 May (evacuated 26 May), and Venice capitulated on 22 August (terms) with Radetzky's entry on 27 August 1849.
wars.note: The page's lead says 28 August, its body and infobox 27 August.

wars.outcome: The Veneto towns rose in March 1848 and were retaken by Austria in June; Venice held out to August 1849.

certainty.note: The mainland towns changed hands week by week and no frontier text exists; only the Venetian lagoon is a firm outline.

notes: New rebel dossier; Cliopatria has no row. Austrian-empire already uses the counterpart slug 'republic-of-san-marco'. Wikidata id not read (wikidata.org unreachable). Pages disagree on dates: independence 22 March (infobox 17 March start of the insurrection); union vote 4 July (this page) vs 5 July (First Italian War page); surrender 22/24/27/28 August 1849. No rulers strip: the page's leadership table shows only Manin as Dictator in August 1848, a triumvirate to March 1849 and Manin as President of the Executive Power from March 1849; the first five months are not given. Belluno and Rovigo return to Austria at confidence 1 (page silent). The mainland holdings are provinces of the modern Veneto, a rough reading of 'towns'.
